topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: The light in the shop was dim, casting long, wavering shadows that seemed to dance on the walls. I traced the glass countertop with my finger, each piece behind it more dazzling than the last. And then, there it was, nestled among trinkets and forgotten treasures—a ring. Not just any ring, but the one that used to sparkle on Grandma’s hand at every family gathering. My heart fluttered against my ribcage, a bird trying to break free from its cage. The pawnbroker’s eyes followed my gaze, curiosity flickering. I cleared my throat, a thin layer of dust settling over my words. “This ring,” I began, my voice barely a whisper, “it belonged to my grandmother.” The shop felt suddenly smaller, the weight of the ring’s history pressing down on me. I reached out, almost afraid to touch it, as if doing so might summon a memory I wasn’t ready to face.
